title: Benefit Overpayment Accounts — Anchoring the Return Look-Back Period
content:
For the returned-payment fee on Benefit Overpayment Accounts, the return look-back period is the number of months, counted back from the handling date, within which the overpayment's return entries are looked at. The return look-back period is anchored according to the overpayment.

## The three anchorings

1. **Overpayment carrying a repayment plan.** For an overpayment carrying a repayment plan, current or defaulted, whose first installment due date has passed, the look-back is anchored at that first installment due date and covers the whole months elapsed from that date to the handling date plus the month in progress.
2. **Fraud overpayment without such a plan.** For a fraud overpayment (Fraud Overpayment — First Offense or Fraud Overpayment — Repeat Offense) without such a plan, the look-back is anchored at the determination date and covers the whole months elapsed from the determination date to the handling date plus the month in progress.
3. **Any other overpayment.** For any other overpayment the look-back runs back the standard look-back months, 12 months, from the handling date.

A first installment due date has passed when it is earlier than the handling date. A plan whose status on the overpayment record is none or completed, or a current or defaulted plan whose first installment due date is the handling date or later, is not such a plan.

## Which anchoring applies

| Plan current or defaulted, first installment due date passed | Fraud classification | Look-back months |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes or no | Whole months from the first installment due date to the handling date, plus one |
| No | Yes | Whole months from the determination date to the handling date, plus one |
| No | No | 12 |

## Worked examples (hypothetical dates)

- A defaulted plan with a first installment due date of 10 January; handling date 25 April. Three whole months have elapsed; the look-back is 4 months.
- A Fraud Overpayment — Repeat Offense account with no plan, determination date 5 March of the previous year; handling date 20 May. Fourteen whole months have elapsed; the look-back is 15 months.
- A Non-Fraud Overpayment — Agency Error account whose current plan has its first installment due date next week: the look-back is 12 months.
